children.title: Email Dos and Don'ts
children.content:
I check my email during any school day from 8 am to 4:30 pm. If an email is sent in the evening or over the weekend, I will respond during the next school day. If you need quick information, it's often better to ask one of your classmates before asking me.

Examples of appropriate emails:
• I am sick and will miss the next 2 classes. What work will I miss?
• I will be absent next week for a family vacation next week during the test. When can I schedule a time to take it?
• Will you be available for tutorials Wednesday morning?
• This assignment says it's due on Friday but accepting submissions until Sunday. Can I get some clarification on this?

Examples of inappropriate emails:
• Can you update my grade in HAC? - If a grade is correct in Schoology but out-of-date in HAC, you can rest assured I will sync your grades in the next few days. At a minimum, I will sync grades on Tuesday mornings and after entering summative grades. There is no need to email me about this.
• What is wrong with my answer on this formative assessment? - We have time for formatives built into class each day. You may ask me for help during class or tutorials.

children.title: guess-the-number.py
children.content:
# This is a guess the number game.
import random
secret_number = random.randint(1, 20)
print('I am thinking of a number between 1 and 20.')

# Ask the player to guess 6 times.
for guesses_taken in range(1, 7):
	print('Take a guess.')
	guess = int(input())

	if guess < secret_number:
		print('Your guess is too low.')
	elif guess > secret_number:
		print('Your guess is too high.')
	else:
		break		# This condition is the correct guess!

if guess == secret_number:
	print('Good job! You guessed my number in', guesses_taken, 'guesses!')
else:
	print('Nope. The number I was thinking of was', secret_number)

import random

NUM_DIGITS = 3
MAX_GUESSES = 10


def main():
	print('''Bagels, a deductive logic game.
by Al Sweigart

I am thinking of a {}-digit number with no repeated digits.
Try to guess waht it is. Here are some clues:

When I say:  That means:
Pico         One digit is correct but in the wrong position.
Fermi        One digit is correct and in the right position.
Bagels       No digit is correct.

For example, if the secret number was 248 and your guess was 843, the
clues would be Fermi Pico.'''.format(NUM_DIGITS))

	while True: # Main game loop
		# This stores the secret number the player needs to guess.
		secret_num = get_secret_num()
		print('I have thought up a number.')
		print('You have {} guesses to get it.'.format(MAX_GUESSES))

		num_guesses = 1
		while num_guesses <= MAX_GUESSES:
			guess = ''
			# Keep looping until they enter a valid guess:
			while len(guess) != NUM_DIGITS or not guess.isdecimal():
				print('Guess #{}: '.format(num_guesses))
				guess = input('> ')

			clues = get_clues(guess, secret_num)
			print(clues)
			num_guesses += 1

			if guess == secret_num:
				break
			if num_guesses > MAX_GUESSES:
				print('YOu ran out of guesses.')
				print('The answer was {}.'.format(secret_num))

		# Ask player if they want to play again.
		print('Do you want to play again? (yes or no)')
		if not input('> ').lower().startswith('y'):
			print('Thanks for playing!')
			break


def get_secret_num():
	"""Returns a string made up of NUM_DIGITS unique random digits."""
	numbers = list('0123456789') # Create a list for the secret number.
	random.shuffle(numbers) # Shuffle them into rnadom order.

	# Get the first NUM_DIGITS digits in the list for the secret number:
	secret_num = ''
	for i in range(NUM_DIGITS):
		secret_num += str(numbers[i])
	return secret_num


def get_clues(guess, secret_num):
	"""Returns a string with the pico, fermi, bagels clues for a guess
		and secret number pair."""
	if guess == secret_num:
		return 'You got it!'

	clues = []

	for i in range(len(guess)):
		if guess[i] == secret_num[i]:
			# A correct digit is in the correct place.
			clues.append('Fermi')
		elif guess[i] in secret_num:
			# A correct digit is in the incorrect place.
			clues.append('Pico')

	if len(clues) == 0:
		return 'Bagels'
	else:
		# Sort the clues into alphabetical order so their original order
		# doesn't give information away.
		clues.sort()
		# Make a single string from the list of string clues.
		return ' '.join(clues)


if __name__ == '__main__':
	main()

import time, sys
indent = 0
indentation_increasing = True

try:
  while True:
    print(' ' * indent, end='')
    print('********')
    time.sleep(0.1)
  
    if indentation_increasing:
      indent += 1
      if indent == 20:
        indentation_increasing = False
    else:
      indent -= 1
      if indent == 0:
        indentation_increasing = True
except KeyboardInterrupt:
  sys.exit()

children.title: Hexadecimal & ASCII
children.content:
Hexadecimal

  • bit - binary digit
  • byte - 8 bits
  • nibble - 4 bits
0000 0 1000 8
0001 1 1001 9
0010 2 1010 A
0011 3 1011 B
0100 4 1100 C
0101 5 1101 D
0110 6 1110 E
0111 7 1111 F

ASCII

ASCII-decimal-binary Chart

Useful Python Functions

  • ord(c) - returns int ASCII value of character c
  • chr(i) - returns character at ASCII value i
  • bin(i) - returns str of int i in binary notation
  • hex(i) - returns str of int i in hexadecimal notation
  • int(s, b) - returns decimal int of string s in base b
